<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919272_theRebbe_883" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919272_theRebbe_883__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Avraham's initial recognition of G-dliness came from observing the world, and that this recognition was publicized through his self-nullification stemming from the level of Yechidah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is also what is continued in the maamar, that the beginning of Avraham's service was the recognition of G-dliness from worldly matters,</t>
    <t s="2">as it is brought in the Midrash23</t>
    <t s="3">a parable of one who was traveling from place to place and saw a palace that was illuminated; he said, "Could it be that this palace has no caretaker?"</t>
    <t s="4">The master of the palace peered out at him, etc.</t>
    <t s="5">So too, because our father Avraham would say, "Could it be that this world has no caretaker?"</t>
    <t s="6">The Holy One, blessed be He, peered out at him and said to him, "I am the Master of the world."</t>
    <t s="7">Now, it can be explained that the matter of "I am the Master of the world" that was revealed to Avraham is the concept of the "Boreh spark" that is clothed in a "created spark,"</t>
    <t s="8">for the created spark in which the "Boreh spark" is clothed is the aspect of Yechidah in the soul, as explained in Etz Chayim24.</t>
    <t s="9">And this recognition of G-dliness he also publicized throughout the entire world,</t>
    <t s="10">as it is written25</t>
    <t s="11">"And he called there in the name of the L-rd, the G-d of the world" — do not read "vayikra" (and he called) but "vayakri" (and he caused others to call)26,</t>
    <t s="12">meaning he caused this to be proclaimed throughout the entire world, that there is a Master of this palace,</t>
    <t s="13">and as explained in many places27</t>
    <t s="14">the precise wording "E-l Olam" (G-d of the world),</t>
    <t s="15">and not "E-l HaOlam" (the G-d of the world),</t>
    <t s="16">meaning not that G-dliness is a separate entity and the world is a separate entity, but rather that G-dliness rules and dominates over the world,</t>
    <t s="17">but rather that the world and G-dliness are entirely one,</t>
    <t s="18">for "there is nothing besides Him"28.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is the connection between Avraham's recognition of G-dliness and his service of trials,</t>
    <t s="20">for the service of trials is through self-sacrifice that stems from the Yechidah in the soul.</t>
    <t s="21">For this is also that Avraham's self-sacrifice was not like the self-sacrifice of Rabbi Akiva who said29</t>
    <t s="22">"When will the opportunity come to me and I will fulfill it,"</t>
    <t s="23">but rather his entire being was to publicize His G-dliness, blessed be He, in the world30,</t>
    <t s="24">except that if self-sacrifice was needed for this, he was prepared for it.</t>
    <t s="25">And this is because our father Avraham had no existence of his own,</t>
    <t s="26">and "I am but dust and ashes"31,</t>
    <t s="27">which is the concept of self-sacrifice that stems from the aspect of Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="28">And specifically from this state of nullification came the greatest strength,</t>
    <t s="29">to the point that even though "Avraham was one"32,</t>
    <t s="30">and "the entire world was on one side and he was on the other side"33,</t>
    <t s="31">nevertheless, "he inherited the land"32,</t>
    <t s="32">meaning he publicized His G-dliness, blessed be He, throughout the entire world,</t>
    <t s="33">through which the world is built to be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms34.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section distinguishes between the service of refinement (birurim), which involves engaging with the object being refined, and the service of trials (nisyonos), which involves the person working on themselves through rejection and nullification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the reason why the service of trials is specifically through self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="2">is explained in the maamar35</t>
    <t s="3">because in a trial, the G-dly spark is most hidden and concealed.</t>
    <t s="4">And it explains, with an introduction, the difference between the service of refinements and the service of trials</t>
    <t s="5">(for even though trials are also part of the service of refinements for which the soul descended below36,</t>
    <t s="6">nevertheless, there is a difference between them),</t>
    <t s="7">for in the service of refinements, the engagement is with the thing being refined,</t>
    <t s="8">like physical food, where the spark is in the food being refined, and the refinement is through engaging with it</t>
    <t s="9">(and so too is it regarding all of a person's needs, which are called by the name "eating"37),</t>
    <t s="10">but not so with a trial, where the manner of its refinement is not through engaging with the thing, but rather through the person's engagement with himself.</t>
    <t s="11">And the concept is,</t>
    <t s="12">that the service of refinements is in a manner of war,</t>
    <t s="13">"bread is eaten on the face of the sword"38.</t>
    <t s="14">This is through the prior preparation of prayer, as it is written39</t>
    <t s="15">"with my sword and with my bow," and the Targum translates, "with my prayer and with my supplication,"</t>
    <t s="16">and as explained in many places40</t>
    <t s="17">regarding the blessings of the Shema</t>
    <t s="18">(which are the introduction to the Shema,</t>
    <t s="19">"And you shall love," etc.,</t>
    <t s="20">the general concept of prayer41)</t>
    <t s="21">which is contemplation on the root of the animal soul and the refinements, etc.,</t>
    <t s="22">through which he refines them, etc.</t>
    <t s="23">Therefore, it is service in a manner of war and clothing oneself in the thing being refined, as he contemplates its root and through this refines it.</t>
    <t s="24">And similarly, it is regarding the general service of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="25">which is through war with the evil inclination,</t>
    <t s="26">where one must argue</t>
    <t s="27">(argue it out)</t>
    <t s="28">and fight with it with all kinds of war strategies, etc., and through contemplation in various ways of how to defeat it.</t>
    <t s="29">But not so regarding the matter of trials, for the service in them is not through elevating them,</t>
    <t s="30">but rather in a manner of rejection and nullification.</t>
    <t s="31">And this is analogous to the difference within the mitzvos themselves between positive commandments and negative commandments.</t>
    <t s="32">For positive commandments, their concept is doing and action,</t>
    <t s="33">meaning that one engages with the thing through which he fulfills the mitzvah</t>
    <t s="34">(with the object and in the object),</t>
    <t s="35">but negative commandments, their concept is "turn away from evil"42,</t>
    <t s="36">meaning he turns away from evil and rejects it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that unlike negative commandments which still relate to the object being refined, the service of trials involves a person's inner strength to nullify a trial that has no true existence, as exemplified by Avraham's binding of Isaac and the Rebbe Rayatz's imprisonment.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, although the manner of service of negative commandments is through rejection and nullification,</t>
    <t s="2">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="3">in this it is comparable to the service of positive commandments,</t>
    <t s="4">for both are in a matter of existence upon which the definition of action and absence of action applies,</t>
    <t s="5">except that in positive commandments one is commanded about action, and in negative commandments about the absence of action.</t>
    <t s="6">Therefore, the engagement in negative commandments is not only with the person himself,</t>
    <t s="7">but also with the thing being refined.</t>
    <t s="8">For although the main service of negative commandments is in that one rules and dominates over his inclination not to eat, etc.,</t>
    <t s="9">which is in a manner of rejection and nullification,</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="11">since his service is with a thing that has existence in physicality and matter,</t>
    <t s="12">he has a connection,</t>
    <t s="13">in a negative manner at least,</t>
    <t s="14">to the thing being refined.</t>
    <t s="15">But not so the service of trials, which is in a matter</t>
    <t s="16">(in the language of the maamar43)</t>
    <t s="17">that is not a thing in its own right, but rather a thing was placed to conceal and prevent,</t>
    <t s="18">and therefore the person's engagement is with himself,</t>
    <t s="19">to arouse his own essential power, which is the strength to stand against the trial,</t>
    <t s="20">and not to be affected by it at all,</t>
    <t s="21">to the point that he does not enter into arguments and responses, but only stands with the strength that it is impossible otherwise, and nullifies the trial completely.</t>
    <t s="22">And through this strength, it is truly nullified, because the truth of the matter is revealed, that it is a thing that has no existence,</t>
    <t s="23">and its entire existence is only so that the essence of his soul should be revealed to the person,</t>
    <t s="24">which is his inner will that is above being clothed in vessels.</t>
    <t s="25">And this is analogous to the trial of Avraham in the trial of the Binding</t>
    <t s="26">(for the main opening of the channel of self-sacrifice through Avraham was in the trial of the Binding44),</t>
    <t s="27">for the main trial was in the matter of alacrity,</t>
    <t s="28">and as explained in Igeres HaKodesh45</t>
    <t s="29">that the alacrity of our father Avraham stands for us forever, etc., until eternity.</t>
    <t s="30">And as our sages, of blessed memory, said46</t>
    <t s="31">that a great river was made before them, etc., and nevertheless Avraham was not affected and went to fulfill his mission from the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="32">and he descended into the water, etc.,</t>
    <t s="33">and through this the existence of the river was nullified,</t>
    <t s="34">for through his strength, the truth was revealed that the entire existence of the river was only to test him, etc.</t>
    <t s="35">And so too afterwards</t>
    <t s="36">(in the trial of the Binding itself)</t>
    <t s="37">that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "I did not tell you... 'I have brought him up, bring him down'"47.</t>
    <t s="38">And similarly was the conduct of the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the master of joy and redemption, during his imprisonment</t>
    <t s="39">(as recounted in his notes48</t>
    <t s="40">and talks49),</t>
    <t s="41">that he decided at its beginning to be strong and firm without fear and not to consider the situation at all, etc.,</t>
    <t s="42">and so was his conduct all the days of his imprisonment,</t>
    <t s="43">and through this,</t>
    <t s="44">not only did this conduct give him the strength to stand against all the difficulties, concealments, and obscurities of the imprisonment</t>
    <t s="45">(the concealment and obscurity were not only regarding his physical matters,</t>
    <t s="46">but also regarding his spiritual matters,</t>
    <t s="47">and it is emphasized that during his imprisonment there was no possibility to engage in spreading Judaism and the wellsprings),</t>
    <t s="48">but furthermore,</t>
    <t s="49">through this the concealment and obscurity were nullified.</t>
    <t s="50">For although initially they appeared to be a strong and great existence</t>
    <t s="51">(as recounted in his notes),</t>
    <t s="52">nevertheless, through his strength they were nullified from their existence,</t>
    <t s="53">to the point that he was freed in a manner revealed to all.</t>
    <t s="54">And through this, there was also an advantage in the master of joy and redemption himself,</t>
    <t s="55">similar to what happened regarding the matter of Yud-Tes Kislev,</t>
    <t s="56">that through the imprisonment and redemption, an elevation was made regarding Chassidus, as explained in many places50,</t>
    <t s="57">so too here51</t>
    <t s="58">that an elevation was made in the master of joy and redemption as mentioned,</t>
    <t s="59">that the service of spreading the Torah increased with greater vigor than before,</t>
    <t s="60">to the point that through this he began, in actuality, the matter of spreading it throughout the entire world,</t>
    <t s="61">and in a manner of "from now and until eternity"52.</t>
    <t s="62">And analogous to what is brought in the Gemara53</t>
    <t s="63">that when there are three generations engaged in Torah, the Torah will no longer cease from his seed, because the Torah seeks its lodging place,</t>
    <t s="64">so too in our matter,</t>
    <t s="65">that there are already</t>
    <t s="66">(as a result of the redemption of Yud-Beis-Yud-Gimmel Tammuz)</t>
    <t s="67">three generations of those who study Torah and fulfill His mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="68">and even more, those who love13</t>
    <t s="69">Torah and His mitzvos</t>
    <t s="70">(through which their fulfillment of mitzvos is with beauty54).</t>
    <t s="71">All this is through his standing with the greatest strength, above all calculations,</t>
    <t s="72">through which he nullified the trial in the most elevated manner.</t>
    <t s="73">And since "the end follows the beginning"55,</t>
    <t s="74">so too must it be in the service of each and every one,</t>
    <t s="75">that we go in the straight path that He has taught us from His ways, and we shall walk in His paths56,</t>
    <t s="76">to stand with strength not to be affected by any obstacles or delays in the service of G-d,</t>
    <t s="77">for since one is going to fulfill his mission in this world,</t>
    <t s="78">the trial has no existence,</t>
    <t s="79">and "the L-rd your G-d tests you to know whether you love the L-rd your G-d"57,</t>
    <t s="80">and through strength and self-sacrifice, the trial is nullified.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
